inconsistencies: Chain: #35861 (Testnet 5) is built on #35793 (BIP 54) and activates its rules from block 1; review #35793 first, decisions there determine #35861.
Chain: #35646 removes M_ERROR from ValidationState and is stated to unblock #35570's return-by-value refactor; review #35646 before #35570.
Chain: #32575 unifies the script-check path and is the stated prerequisite for #29491's batch verification; it was scored below the PR it unblocks, hence the promotion to P2. Review #32575 first.
Chain: #35731 builds on #35714; #35714 carries the actual corruption-prevention fix, so review it first and treat #35731 as the hardening follow-up.

Overlapping problem area: #34132, #35003, #35714, #36049 and #35646 all rework fatal storage/IO error handling in validation and blockstorage, from different layers (dbwrapper point reads, FlatFileSeq::Open, flush return values, buffered-writer termination, error-type separation). They will conflict and the approach dispute raised on #35003 (exceptions vs nullable returns) affects the others; a single architectural decision should be taken across them, starting with #34132/#35714.

Overlapping proposals of the same kind: #31989 (CTV), #32247 (CSFS), #29247 (CAT), #36122 (CISA) are all regtest-or-flag-only implementations of proposed consensus rules; they were banded inconsistently (one P1, two P2, one P3) when their consequence within validation is the same class. Normalized to P2 (P3 for the explicitly not-for-merge CISA draft).

#36598 proposes removing AssumeUTXO entirely while #35054, #36603, #36633, #36543, #36542, #36500, #35307 and #36346 all invest in it. A direction decision on #36598 changes the value of that whole group; it is a demo PR, so the decision should be taken in discussion rather than letting it displace the concrete assumeutxo fixes.
#36361 is a deliberate backport of already-merged #35168 to the 31.x branch; it duplicates merged master work by design and should be judged only on the release-branch crash it fixes.
#35751 and #36496 both modify CoinsViewOverlay prevout prefetching introduced in #35295; they touch the same code and should be reviewed together, #35751 first since it carries the measured benefit.

Modularization cluster: #35906, #36066, #35569 and #35187 all serve the stateless validation library idea in #35904; none states a dependency order, but reviewing #35906 first establishes the shape the others assume.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: a small P1 set of crashes, data loss and a shipped regression; a broad P2 set mixing storage-error correctness, measured IBD/pruning/snapshot performance, and proposed-consensus-rule implementations; a long P3 tail of narrow fixes, hardening and modularization steps. Within P2 I put demonstrated defects and measured speedups ahead of the soft-fork implementations, since the latter are regtest-only and their value is reaching a decision rather than shipping behavior. Several P3 placements moved up or down by more than five because the original scores ordered small bug fixes below refactors of similar or lesser certainty.
